query: Compare optical and SAR backscatter for built-up structures and water
answer: The comparison reveals a strong correlation between optical and SAR signatures for land-use classification. The grid-patterned urban/built-up zone (top right) in the optical image (Image 1) demonstrates high-frequency geometric structure. In the corresponding SAR imagery (Image 2), this region exhibits high backscatter intensity (bright white speckles) due to the 'double-bounce' effect off building structures and rough surfaces. Conversely, the dark, smooth blue-shaded area in the bottom right of Image 1—suggesting water or a specular surface—corresponds to very low backscatter (near-black) in Image 2. This is characteristic of specular reflection in SAR, where microwave energy is reflected away from the sensor, confirming a smooth surface geometry.
